name: Lazarus Emergency Response Triage Coverall
description:
Lazarus emergency response teams deploy to mass-casualty events, industrial accidents, and — in practice — anywhere that Lazarus has a contractual obligation to provide care, which covers a significant portion of GLMZ's mid and lower tiers. The triage coverall is a single-piece garment in Lazarus white with high-visibility red banding at the shoulders, wrists, and ankles. The fabric is a triple-layer biohazard-rated membrane that resists biological fluid penetration at Level 2 classification, with sealed seams and integrated glove attachment rings at the cuffs. Chest and thigh pockets are sized and labeled for specific equipment: airway kit, compression wraps, diagnostic scanner, and a pouch for Lazarus-issued pharmacological emergency tabs.

The coverall is designed with full augment compatibility: dorsal panels open via breakaway seams for responders with spinal chrome, and port-access panels at the forearms allow field diagnostics through wrist-jack interfaces without removing the suit. Geneware accommodations are limited — tail openings exist in the base pattern, but horn and ear clearance requires a custom order that takes three weeks and costs an additional Φ90. Most responders with significant geneware modifications carry their own aftermarket modification kits. The coverall is disposable by Lazarus protocol after significant biohazard exposure, though many the Gray Zone-based responders clean and reuse them out of necessity.
cultural_context: Lazarus triage coveralls are a dual symbol in GLMZ — hope in crisis situations, and a reminder that emergency medical care in the city is a service delivered by a corponation with a billing department. the Gray Zone residents who have experienced Lazarus response sometimes describe the sight of the white-and-red coveralls as simultaneously reassuring and ominous. The coveralls circulate secondhand in Tier 1 markets as general-purpose protective workwear.
story_hooks: A character in a Lazarus coverall is the only medical responder on scene at an incident that Lazarus has officially declined to cover under contract.
Secondhand triage coveralls from a specific batch have been modified to carry a concealed payload — someone is using the Lazarus brand as cover for distribution.
A responder's coverall contains field notes written in the lining about a mass-casualty event that was never publicly reported.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stark white single-piece coverall with bold red banding at shoulders, wrists, and ankles. Clean, clinical silhouette that reads as both medical authority and corporate efficiency. The high-visibility striping creates a sharp, almost institutional aesthetic that commands attention in chaotic environments.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not form-fitting—designed for layering over light augmentation and allowing full range of motion during emergency response. Relaxed through the torso, tapered slightly at wrists and ankles where the red banding cinches. Shoulders slightly structured to accommodate dorsal panel breakaway seams.
physical_description.primary_material: Triple-layer biohazard-rated membrane composite. Medical-grade synth-polymer with sealed seams throughout. Outer layer has a subtle matte finish that resists fluid sheening.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost slick surface with micro-ridged seams visible under close inspection. The red banding has slightly higher friction than the white base. Integrated glove attachment rings feel rigid and precise at the cuffs.
physical_description.color_scheme: Clinical white as primary, with high-visibility red-orange banding at shoulders (full width), wrists (2cm band), and ankles (2cm band). Subtle Lazarus logo in matte red on left chest. Equipment pocket labels in minimal black stencil.
physical_description.closures: Full-length magnetic seal down the center front, reinforced with friction-fit tabs. Breakaway seams at dorsal panels (designed to separate under pressure without full removal). Port-access panels at forearms secured with medical-grade magnetic clasps.
distinctive_features: Sealed seams throughout for biohazard Level 2 rating
Integral pharmacological pouch on right hip
Glove attachment rings (silicone-grip) at both cuffs
Dorsal panel breakaway seams for spinal augmentation access
Forearm port-access panels for wrist-jack diagnostics
Optional custom tail/horn/ear modifications (aftermarket or special order)
Minimal branding—Lazarus wordmark only, no corporate flourish
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 corporate-issue. The precision construction and biohazard certification mark it as higher-grade than street wear, but the emphasis on function over aesthetics keeps it accessible to working-class responders.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Lazarus emergency response personnel across mid and lower-tier GLMZ. Signals both medical authority and corporate extraction of crisis labor. Circulates secondhand in Tier 1 markets as durable protective workwear. Deeply ambiguous in the Gray Zone culture—reassurance and dread combined.
physical_description.condition_typical: Varies sharply: pristine when fresh from Lazarus supply (rarely seen past first deployment), or heavily stained with dried biological matter and field repairs. Many reused coveralls show bleach marks, tape patches on sealed seams, and faded red banding. Disposal protocol is often circumvented by lower-tier responders who treat them as reusable gear.
